finding: The use case determines which features and populations are legitimate; 'identify diabetes' alone is ambiguous
evidence_value: use case = screening aid applied before any glucose test
decision: Frame the question as non-glycaemic identification of adult diabetes (diagnosed or not) with a screening use case; models are measuring instruments, not the product
alternatives_rejected: Pure prediction benchmark on all variables; causal question
check_note: Question and use case restated from the process document; scope sections checked against S1 step 1

finding: The training target must be fixed before modelling and be reproducible
evidence_value: N=5730; L_self 819; L_A1c 721; L_comb 971 (16.9% unweighted, 14.0% WTPH2YR, CI 12.4-15.6)
decision: Freeze L_comb = DIQ010==1 or LBXGH>=6.5 on adults >=20, examined, non-pregnant; DIQ010=3 coded negative and flagged (target-freeze happens after S5)
alternatives_rejected: L_A1c only (loses controlled diabetics); L_self only (misses undiagnosed)
check_note: Counts 819/721/971 and prevalences recomputed from raw files and asserted in section 1

finding: 84% of L_comb positives already report a diagnosis, so a whole-cohort AUC mostly measures recognising known patients
decision: Report E-ALL and E-SCREEN as co-primary populations; the gap between them is a headline finding
check_note: Strata 569/250/152/4759 recomputed with src.labels and asserted

finding: Leakage must be decided by one rule, not variable by variable
evidence_value: 14 inadmissible, 13 Tier-1 and 2 Tier-2 variables in the S1 draft; spec agrees on all shared variables
decision: Admit a feature only if available at the screening moment, not a diagnostic criterion, not a diagnosis consequence, not derived from the target; N for LBXGH, LBXGLU, DIQ010, DIQ050, DIQ070, DID040, DID060, DIQ160, DIQ180
alternatives_rejected: Judging leakage per variable by impression; keeping DIQ070 because it is asked of some undiagnosed respondents
check_note: Draft table asserted against must-be-N/T1/T2 lists and cross-checked with variable_spec.csv (0 disagreements)

finding: BPQ020 and BPQ080 are legitimate questionnaire items but traces of earlier health-care contact
decision: Keep them admissible and add a T1-minus-care ablation arm reported on E-ALL and E-SCREEN
alternatives_rejected: Drop them silently from T1; ignore the issue
check_note: Spec flags exactly the two admissible variables (asserted)

finding: Race, insurance and usual place of care raise fairness and access-to-care questions
evidence_value: RIDRETH3, HIQ011, HUQ030 have role audit
decision: Exclude from models by default; use as audit and stratification variables
alternatives_rejected: Include race as predictor; ignore for fairness
check_note: Spec role audit set equals {RIDRETH3, HIQ011, HUQ030} (asserted)

finding: The ADA risk score cannot be reproduced: family history and gestational diabetes are not collected in this cycle
evidence_ref: Section 1 (ADA-lite baseline); CDC codebooks MCQ_L and DIQ_L
evidence_value: 5 of 7 items available; 0 codebook hits for 'family history', 'blood relative', 'gestational'
decision: Use ADA-lite (reduced version, missing 2 items), compared on E-SCREEN only; report AUC plus sensitivity and PPV at the 35% screened fraction of Bang 2009
alternatives_rejected: Claim an ADA score replication; use a proxy for family history
check_note: Codebook text search run in section 1; Bang AUC 0.79 vs 0.83 flagged [to verify]

finding: Hypotheses must state metric, direction, magnitude, SESOI, falsifier and prior exposure to be falsifiable and honest
decision: Draft H1a-H4b with prior_exposure markers; only H2b, H2c and H3 claim true pre-registration; ownership passes to S6, locked by SHA-256 at prereg-lock
alternatives_rejected: Call S3-S5 findings pre-registered; leave fields empty
check_note: Table parsed from hypotheses.md; ids, seven fields and prior_exposure vocabulary asserted

finding: Overclaiming novelty is penalised in review and is not supportable
decision: State the contribution as a combination applied to one cycle with fixed basic models; no priority or superlative claims; integration not found in consulted literature [to verify]
alternatives_rejected: Claim to be the first to show Asian low-BMI or access gaps

finding: NCHS DUA forbids linkage and disclosure-method research and constrains external validation
decision: Validate externally only against published aggregates (DB516, Bang 2009); take top-coding as given; flag n<30, effective n<30, CI width>=0.30, df<8
alternatives_rejected: Linking to external individual-level data; testing re-identification
check_note: Obligation table rendered; no external microdata in repository

finding: Disclosure controls in the public files shape variables and variance estimation
evidence_value: age 80 top-code 321 (5.6%); PIR top-code 1282 (22.4%); PIR missing 734 (12.8%); 15 strata, 30 PSU, df 15
decision: Keep age_top, pir_top and pir_miss indicators; jackknife with design df 15; never try to undo controls
alternatives_rejected: Treat top-coded values as measurements; hide missing income
check_note: Counts recomputed from the cohort and raw DEMO_L and asserted

finding: Weights and a low response rate limit generalisation; the cycle has no oversampling so subgroups are thin
evidence_value: response 34.6% interview, 25.7% MEC (NCHS); 60+ share 46.2% sample vs 31.4% weighted; Kish deff 1.55; Asian n=315 (50 positives)
decision: Use WTPH2YR for cohort analyses, state the no-oversampling and non-response caveats, label Asian results exploratory
alternatives_rejected: Report unweighted prevalence only; pool cycles to enlarge subgroups
check_note: Shares, Kish deff and Asian counts recomputed and asserted; response rates are NCHS-published, not computable

finding: The H1a interval for the uninsured undiagnosed share in the design draft (24.9-61.2) differs from the S5 Korn-Graubard interval (24.8-62.7, width 0.38)
decision: Keep the risk difference with lower CI bound >0 as the formal criterion; the share is exploratory; S5 recomputes the values
check_note: Reconciliation is verified in S5, not in S1

finding: Keeping columns without an analytic purpose is a minimisation risk even for public data
evidence_value: 175 raw columns in 16 files: 78 kept, 97 dropped (55%); dropped include country of birth, years in the US, military service, household-size details
decision: Keep only columns the variable specification marks include; drop the rest at load time with a stated reason per column
alternatives_rejected: Load everything and ignore unused columns
check_note: Report totals recomputed and asserted in section 1 (kept + dropped = raw columns)
